                                    I.      INTRODUCTION

Question No. 1: Please state your name and address for the record.

Answer: My name is David O. Carpenter, and my address is 2749 Old State Road
Schenectady, New York 12303.

Question No. 2: On whose behalf are you testifying in this proceeding?

Answer: On behalf of the E6 Link Intervenors, represented by Grissom & Thompson LLP,
affected by the E6 route for the 765-kV line known as the "Bell County East to Big Hill
765-kV Transmission Project".

Question No. 3: Have you ever testified in any other proceeding before the Public Utility
Commission?

Answer: Not before the Texas Public Utility Commission, although I have testified before
other utility commissions. I have prepared a list of matters in which I have testified, which
is attached as Exhibit A.

We offer Exhibit A into evidence.

                             II.        PURPOSE OF TESTIMONY

Question No. 4: What topics were you asked to evaluate for this proceeding?

Answer: I was asked to evaluate and provide opinions regarding the potential human
health effects associated with exposure to electromagnetic fields ("EMFs") generated by
high-voltage transmission lines. Specifically, I was asked to evaluate the scientific and
medical literature concerning whether prolonged exposure to EMFs may be associated
with adverse health effects.
I was also asked to evaluate whether the number of homes and residents located in close
proximity to a proposed transmission line route is relevant from a public health
perspective, and whether prudent public health policy supports minimizing the number
of individuals exposed to EMFs where reasonably feasible alternative routes are
available.

Question No. 5: What is your background?




                                              6
 Answer: I am a public health physician and environmental health scientist with decades
of experience studying the effects of environmental exposures on human health,
including exposure to electromagnetic fields ("EMFs"). I currently serve as the Vincent
O'Leary Professor of Environmental Health Sciences in the College of Integrated Health
Sciences at the University at Albany, State University of New York, and as Co-Director of
the Institute for Health and the Environment, which has been designated as a
Collaborating Centre of the World Health Organization. I also serve as an Honorary
Professor at the Queensland Children's Medical Research Institute at the University of
Queensland in Brisbane, Australia.
I received my Bachelor of Arts degree from Harvard College, graduating magna cum
laude, and my Medical Degree from Harvard Medical School, graduating cum laude.
Throughout my career, I have held numerous academic, research, and public health
leadership positions, including serving as Chairman of the Neurobiology Department at
the Armed Forces Radiobiology Research Institute, Director of the Wadsworth Center for
Laboratories and Research for the New York State Department of Health, and Dean of the
School of Public Health at the University at Albany.
My professional work has included extensive research and analysis relating to ionizing
and non-ionizing radiation, environmental contaminants, and public health policy. I also
served as Executive Secretary for the New York State Power Lines Project a major
research initiative evaluating the health effects associated with power-line
electromagnetic fields.
I have authored or co-authored more than 500 peer-reviewed publications, including
numerous publications, reports, and book chapters concerning EMFs and human health.
I have testified and lectured nationally and internationally regarding EMFs and potential
health impacts associated with exposure to high-voltage transmission lines, including
testimony before committees of the United States House of Representatives and the
President's Cancer Panel concerning EMF exposure and cancer risks.

Question No. 6: What is your current occupation?

Answer: I currently serve as Co-Director of the Institute for Health and the Environment
at the University at Albany. The Institute has been designated as a Collaborating Centre
of the World Health Organization in Environmental Health. I am also the Vincent
O'Leary Professor of Environmental Health Sciences in the College of Integrated Health
Sciences at the University at Albany. In addition, I am an Honorary Professor at the
Queensland Children's Medical Research Institute, University of Queensland, Brisbane,
Australia.




                                           7
 My work focuses on environmental health, including the effects of environmental
contaminants and electromagnetic fields ("EMFs") on human health. Throughout my
career, I have conducted research, published peer-reviewed articles, participated in
public health policy initiatives, and provided expert analysis concerning the health effects
associated with environmental exposures, including exposure to EMFs generated by
high-voltage transmission lines.

Question 7: I am showing you what has been marked as Exhibit B. What is that
document?

Answer: It is my Curriculum Vitae.

Question No. 8: Did you prepare this document?

Answer: Yes.

Question No. 9: Is the information on your Curriculum Vitae true and correct?

Answer: Yes.

We offer Exhibit B into evidence.

Question 10: I am showing you what has been marked as Exhibit C. What is this
document?

Answer: It is a compilation of my publications, books, and other writings relating to
electromagnetic fields ("EMFs"), public health, and associated health effects.

Question 11: Did you prepare this docurnent?

Answer: Yes.

We offer Exhibit C into evidence.

Question No. 12: What did you do to form an opinion in this case?

Answer: In forming my opinions in this matter, I reviewed materials relating to the
proposed transmission line project including the Applicant's application materials, route
information, and information identifying the number of habitable structures associated
with the E6 route and alternative proposed routes.


                                             8
 I also reviewed materials concerning the proximity of residences and communities to the
proposed transmission line routes, as well as scientific and medical literature regarding
potential health effects associated with exposure to electromagnetic fields ("EMFs") from
high-voltage transmission lines.
In addition, I reviewed peer-reviewed publications, prior studies, public health materials,
and other information relevant to the potential human health impacts associated with
prolonged EMF exposure.

Question No. 13: Is the methodology you followed and the materials you reviewed and
relied upon the type reasonably relied upon by physicians, public health professionals,
environmental health scientists, and researchers in your field?

Answer: Yes. The methodology and materials I relied upon in forming my opinions in
this matter are the types of methodologies and materials reasonably relied upon by
experts in the fields of medicine, public health, environmental health sciences,
epidemiology, and electromagnetic field ("EMF") research.
In forming my opinions, I reviewed the Applicant's application materials, route
information, habitable structure data, scientific and medical literature, peer-reviewed
publications, prior studies, and other materials relevant to the potential health effects
associated with exposure to EMFs from high-voltage transmission lines. I also relied
upon my education, training, research, professional experience, and prior work involving
environmental exposures and EMF-related public health issues.
Experts in my field routinely rely upon these types of materials and methodologies when
evaluating potential public health impacts associated with environmental exposures and
transmission line projects.

Question No. 14: What opinions did you arrive at in this case?

Answer: Based upon my education, training, professional experience, review of the
scientific and medical literature, and review of the materials provided in this proceeding,
I arrived at several opinions.
First, it is my opinion that there is substantial scientific literature discussing potential
adverse health effects associated with prolonged exposure to electromagnetic fields
("EMFs") generated by high-voltage transmission lines. In particular, numerous studies
and publications have reported potential associations between EMF exposure and
increased risks of certain illnesses, including childhood leukemia and other adverse
health conditions.
Second, it is my opinion that prudent public health policy supports minimizing
unnecessary exposure to EMFs where reasonably feasible alternatives are available. From



                                             9
 a public health perspective, the number of residences and individuals located in close
proximity to a proposed transmission line route is an important consideration.
Third, it is my opinion that the E6 route impacts a substantially larger number of
habitable structures and residents than certain alternative routes. As a result the E6 route
would expose a greater number of individuals and families to the potential risks and
concerns associated with prolonged EMF exposure.
Accordingly, it is my opinion that from a public health perspective, routes that minimize
the number of impacted homes and residents are preferable where feasible alternatives
exist.

Question 15: I am showing what has been marked as Exhibit D. Do you recognize this
document?

Answer: Yes. It is my report.

Question No. 16: Is Exhibit D a true and correct copy of your report?

Answer: Yes.

Question No. 17: Did you prepare the report?

Answer: Yes.

Question No. 18: Are the opinions you have expressed in this proceeding held to a
reasonable degree of scientific and professional certainty based on the presently available
scientific literature and information reviewed in this matter?

Answer: Yes.

Question No. 19: Are the opinions you have expressed in this proceeding based upon
your education, training, experience, research, and professional judgment and do they
accurately reflect your findings and conclusions?

Answer: Yes.

Offer Exhibit D into evidence.

Question No. 20: Does this conclude your testimony?

Answer: Yes.

WHAT ARE THE HEALTH EFFECTS OF EXTREMELY-LOW FREQUENCY
ELECTROMAGNETIC FIELDS (ELF-EMFs)?

All EMFs have energy and the level of energy increases with frequency. Because
of this ELF EMFs might be expected to be less harmful than those EMFs at higher
frequencies. However, there is strong evidence that excessive exposure to ELF
frequencies contributes to and cause human disease.

The first convincing report of human harm from ELF-EMFs came from Wertheimer
and Leeper (1979) who reported that children living in homes that had high
magnetic fields coming from the neighborhood power lines had higher rates of
Ieukemia than did children living in homes where the magnetic fields were low.
The electric field did not appear to have this effect. They did not directly measure
the magnetic field but developed a "wire code" method of determining relative
intensity of the magnetic field. In addition to distance of the powerline to the house,
they considered the thickness of the wire, because a thick wire reflected a line
carrying high currents. This report was published in the American Journal of
Epidemiology, a very respected journal. This was the publication that triggered the
New York State Powerlines Project which I was responsible for administrating.
One of the projects (Savits et al., 1988) was an attempt to replicate the
Wertheimer and Leeper findings in the same locality using better methods and
with direct measurement of the magnetic fields. The finding of elevated Ieukemia
in children living in homes with high magnetic fields was confirmed both by
applying the wire code method of Wertheimer and Leeper and by direct
measurement of the magnetic fields.

Many of the studies of exposure to magnetic fields and childhood Ieukemia have
been related to residential exposure to neighborhood powerlines, not high voltage
powerlines. This was the case of the study supported by the New York Powerlines
Project that I administered (Savits et al., 1988). But some have studied
residences near to high voltage lines.

Much of the evidence for Ieukemia in children from ELF-EMF exposure comes

 statistically significant 1.25-fold elevated risk of breast cancer in post- menopausal
women.

Overall, the weight of the scientific research shows that magnetic fields increase
the risk of at least Ieukemia, brain and breast cancers in adults, as well as
Ieukemia in children. It is very difficult to get good exposure assessment in large
groups of people to ELF-EMFs since there are so many different sources and
humans move around in their environment. Behrens et al. (2004) showed that
much of the ELF exposure to adults comes from household appliances, and that
this factor results in gross underestimation of total exposure in studies that only
look at powerlines or transformers. As with any other hazardous exposure one
would expect that the level of harm will be a function of the intensity of all
aggregate exposures and the duration of exposures Because it is so difficult to do
an accurate exposure assessment for ELF exposure, I consider excessive ELF
exposure to be a general carcinogen, increasing the risk of all kinds of cancer.

It is not only cancer risk that is increase upon ELF exposure. There is also a
building body of evidence that neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's
are elevated among people with excessive ELF exposure. For Alzheimer's
disease, Qiu et al. (2004) and Feychting et al. (2003) found a statistically
significant elevated risk with ELF-EMF exposure, approximately two or three times
the incidence in a control population. Roosli et al. (2007) looked at neuro-
degenerative diseases among Swiss railway employees exposed to magnetic
fields. For every 10 pT years of cumulative exposure the authors found
Alzheimer's disease risk to increase by 9.4%. No elevated risk was found for
Parkinson's disease or multiple sclerosis. Garcia et al. (2008) analyzed 14
different studies of EMF exposure and Alzheimer's disease and found a consistent
pattern of elevated risk. Huss et al. (2008) reported on deaths from
neurodegenerative diseases among Swiss people who live near to power lines.
They found a dose-dependent increase in risk of Alzheimer's Disease. People
living within 50 m of a power line had a 1.51-fold increased risk of Alzheimer's
after five years residence and this increased to 1.78-fold after 10 years and 2-fold
after 15 years.
In addition to cancer there is a large body of information showing that excessive
exposures to both ELF and RF can in some people lead to the development of a
syndrome called electrical hypersensitivity (EHS), characterized by "brain fog",
headache, fatigue, tinnitus, photophobia and other relatively non-specific symptoms.
The evidence supporting these statements are summarized in the Bioinitiative Report
and the publication by Belpomme et al. (2018). While most publications have
focused on RF exposure, one of the best studies specifically of ELF exposure and
EHS is that of McCarty et al. (2011). They studied a 35-year-old woman physician
who suffered from EHS in a laboratory where she did not know whether or not a 60
Hz electric field was being applied. She reported symptoms of headache and pain
more frequently in the presence of the field in a statistically significant manner.


WHAT IS A "SAFE" DISTANCE FROM A HIGH VOLTAGE POWERLINE?


                                            -9
 The specific issue in this case is what is the distance from a powerline that can be
considered to be "safe". This is not a question for which there is an easy answer.
Each powerline varies in voltage, how much current it carries (which can vary with
time of day), how high the poles carrying the wires are and therefore what distance
from the center of the powerline will show elevated magnetic fields. The critical
factor is the distance from the center of the powerline at which the level of
magnetic field returns to background. In the Swedish studies this was 300 meters
(984.3 feet) for 220 and 400 kV lines. The proposed line in this case is 765 kV, as
was the line here in New York that triggered the New York State Powerlines
Project. While there are 77 families, which includes children and children yet to be
born living within 500 feet of the line, the Swedish report found elevated magnetic
fields at nearly twice that distance. In addition the proposed line will be at 765 kV,
not the 220 or 400 kV as in the Swedish studies, which may well carry more
current, and therefore results in elevated magnetic fields at even a greater
distance. Powerlines should not be built so as to increase the magnetic field level
in any home, especially because most people spend many hours at home each
day. Risk of cancer and other diseases is a function of the level of exposure, the
multiple sources of exposure and the duration to which humans are exposed. The
big problem with powerlines and residential exposure is that unlike that from
appliances the exposure will be continuous for many hours per day.


CONCLUSIONS:

Exposure of humans to elevated magnetic fields causes cancer, especially leukemia in
children but also other cancers in adults and elevates risk of other diseases such as
Alzheimer' s and a syndrome of electro-hypersensitivity. There is strong evidence that
individuals living close to high voltage powerlines have elevated rates of these diseases It
is critical that the proposed 765 kV powerline between Oncor Electric Delivery Company's
existing Bell County East Switch and a new Big Hill substation, expected to run some 214
to 248 miles, be routed so as to impact the fewest possible residences. This is essential to
protect the health of the residents of the 77 homes located within 500 feet of the proposed
E6 line. There are alternative routes the must be selected. It will also help protect the
utilities from further litigation when the parents of children living with 500 feet of the
propose high voltage powerline sue when the child develops leukemia within five years of
operation of the power line.

The conclusions in this report are based on my medical and public health training, my
experience in study of human health effects of electromagnetic fields and upon review of
other relevant publications.
